items.item: The garment views preserve the selected style identities, relaxed proportions, neckline, opening, hem, pocket and band decisions across flat-lays and wearing situations.
The images implement the craft sheet's material applications, colours, size-M proportions, replaceable cuffs and repair placements without contradicting the fixed client records.
The three styles read as a coordinated autumn-and-winter wardrobe; unspecified neckline, hem and pocket decisions remain open but form one coherent family.
Material colours, M01 surface structure and patch construction agree with the craft sheet and collection back view across both repair states and the material images.
The palette links all three style colours to M01 and M02, and the enlarged texture study represents the same M01 used on bodies, sleeves and elbow patches.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Where knit surfaces are resolved, M01 has a double moss structure and M02 has paired knit-and-purl rib columns at a compatible fine-gauge scale. Bodies, sleeves and patches use M01; cuffs and neckline, hem and cardigan opening bands use M02. Surfaces have a washed, unbrushed character. View distance and lighting may reduce detail, but a clearly different stitch structure or brushed pile fails. Any printed material records must agree with the fixed composition, gauge, weights and usable widths; those physical properties need not be inferred from a photograph.

Each of the three label enlargements is associated with its own garment and represents an inside centre-back-neck label, with the collection name above the repair message. The label represents a 75 × 20 mm component; enlargement for readability is allowed. Reversed line order, a missing garment label, an exterior label location or contradictory dimensions fails.

P01 and C01 cuff interfaces, wherever exposed or explained, support removal by undoing hand linking around the sleeve opening. An enlarged interface must allow access to linking-yarn ends inside the sleeve seam. Ordinary wearing views may conceal those ends. Integral knitting, a cut-off sleeve, a zipper or another incompatible replacement mechanism fails.
Resolved attachment stitches on either patch colour are Navy. Lighting and small-scale loss of stitch detail are allowed; clearly contrasting stitch yarn in another colour fails.

The sheet establishes COMMON LOOP and all three style and both material IDs. It records 80% wool/20% nylon and 12 gauge for both materials; M01 double moss, 380 g/m², 1400 mm width and 8 × 8 mm repeat; M02 2 × 2 rib, 420 g/m² and 1000 mm width; both washed and unbrushed. It assigns Rust #9B513D to P01, Navy #253544 to C01 and Cream #E6DDCA to V01. Size-M chest/body/underarm-sleeve values are P01 1120/640/480 mm, C01 1280/720/460 mm and V01 1200/670 mm with sleeve fields inapplicable. P01/C01 cuffs are 240 mm around and 60 mm deep. The sheet specifies matching-yarn linked seams, removable hand-linked matching M02 cuffs, two M01 patches per sleeved style, correct patch colours and 80 × 100 mm geometry centred 180 mm above the cuff seam, removable vertical Navy running stitches at 5/5/10/5 mm, the 75 × 20 mm two-line inside-back-neck label and five 18 mm corozo buttons. Tables or prose are acceptable; missing or contradictory records fail.

Each image prints the IDs relevant to its depicted garments and material applications, agreeing with the craft sheet. Collection views and the palette identify all three styles and both materials; P01 flat-lays identify P01, M01 and M02; elbow details identify P01 and M01; the texture study identifies M01 and its stated style applications. Labels may use callouts or a key. Unrelated IDs need not appear; missing applicable IDs or incorrect assignments fail.

The presentation contains COMMON LOOP, P01, C01, V01, M01 and M02 with the same garment and material meanings established in the craft sheet. The identifiers may be distributed across pages; an omitted identifier or reassigned meaning fails.

Both collection views label each style's size-M chest/body measurements: P01 1120/640 mm, C01 1280/720 mm and V01 1200/670 mm. Enlarged P01 views carry its corresponding garment measurements, including the 480 mm underarm-to-cuff-seam sleeve length. Every flat-lay depicting P01 or C01 labels the relevant cuff as 240 mm joining circumference and 60 mm deep. An associated key is acceptable; missing values, disagreement with the craft sheet or circumference/width confusion fails.

Readable presentation content repeats the sheet's size-M chest/body pairs of P01 1120/640 mm, C01 1280/720 mm and V01 1200/670 mm. A legible reused specification page or a new table is acceptable; omissions, swapped style associations or numerical changes fail.

Garment identities retain their assigned Rust, Navy and Cream body-and-rib colours across these images. The palette links the three style colours and their supplied codes to M01 and M02. The front collection view shows exactly five corozo cardigan buttons with an 18 mm size indication and three legible label enlargements containing both required lines. Natural lighting shifts are acceptable; changed style colours, an incorrect button count or unreadable label wording fails.

A presentation label page makes COMMON LOOP and Made to be mended readable as the label's first and second lines. Its style-colour information preserves Rust P01, Navy C01 and Cream V01. A reused enlargement is acceptable; a missing label page, altered wording or inconsistent colour assignment fails.

The M01 study communicates its 8 × 8 mm double moss repeat, which remains compatible in scale and structure across resolved garment and patch surfaces. Both back flat-lays annotate patches as 80 mm across the sleeve by 100 mm along it, centred on the back sleeve line 180 mm above the cuff joining seam. Repair views communicate patch size. Perspective and fabric deformation may vary; a changed repeat, misplaced patch or missing required back-view dimensions fails.

Presentation content legibly gives the patch's 80 × 100 mm size and centre position 180 mm above the cuff joining seam, agreeing with the specifications and back views. Reused annotated images are sufficient when readable; an absent dimension or a measurement to the patch edge instead of its centre fails.

The same Rust P01 elbow appears with its Cream patch secured and then removed beside the intact exposed attachment area. Sleeve geometry, knit and attachment position agree. The attached detail labels vertical removable running stitches with 5 mm stitches, 5 mm gaps, 10 mm row spacing and 5 mm edge inset. A changed component, missing loose patch, damaged opening or incorrect annotation fails.

Each document independently states that patch stitches run vertically along the sleeve and gives 5 mm stitch length, 5 mm gap, 10 mm row spacing and 5 mm edge inset. Text, tables or legible diagrams are acceptable; any omitted value or changed direction fails.

The three images show an adult seated at home in P01; P01 beneath V01 beneath an open C01 at the office; and P01 beneath a closed C01 while walking on an everyday journey. The office image exposes all three distinct neckline or opening shapes and at least one Cream P01 patch and one Rust C01 patch. Settings and poses may vary within those situations; missing states, incorrect layering or concealed office details fail.

Review the whole video for a 12-second duration and the office outfit performing standing, reaching for a desk item and walking. P01 remains beneath V01 beneath open C01, retaining three discernible neckline or opening shapes, assigned garment colours and compatible M01 texture wherever resolved. The closing frame legibly names COMMON LOOP, P01, C01 and V01. Camera movement is allowed; missing actions, changed garments, incorrect duration or an unreadable or incomplete closing frame fails.

Merely naming a source, substituting unrelated imagery or omitting a source or video still fails.
